newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast prods fall with futures, low demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast prods fall with futures, low demand.

text.p: Wholesale prices for U.S. West Coast refined products dropped sharply Thursday, in line with lower futures markets and weak demand, traders said.
Prices fell 2.00 to 3.00 cents a gallon after sellers cut prices early, reflecting ample unleaded gasoline supply and 46-cent-a-barrel drop in July crude oil on the NYMEX.
"The market is devoid of buyers. Everyone seems to have gas," one trader said.
NYMEX refined products also fell, with July unleaded gasoline 59.82 cents a gallon, off 0.60 cents. Heating oil futures slid 0.84 cents a gallon to 53.32 cents.
Traders said two cargoes of low sulphur diesel fuel left San Francisco for Asia earlier this week, but the volume, 500,000 barrels, was not significant enough to constrain supply.
"Exports aren't going to have an effect," the trader said.
Offers of Los Angeles regular CARB-grade cleaner burning gasoline dropped two cents to 60 cents a gallon Thursday.
San Francisco CARB gasoline was pegged about two cents gallon lower as well, and fell one cent under LA grades.
Prompt regular unleaded gasoline in Los Angeles was offered at 57.50 cents, 1.50 cents cents lower than Wednesday, traders said.
CARB diesel fuel slid three cents a gallon to 60/61 cents.
